a:r.a:t: Why is Rift so much faster? It comes down to the fundamental difference between interpreted and native code.
Mountebank runs on Node.js. That means every request goes through the V8 JavaScript engine. V8 is remarkably fast for JavaScript, but it still has:
- Garbage collection pauses that can spike latency
- JIT compilation warmup that makes cold starts slow
- A single-threaded event loop that limits CPU utilization
- Parsing JSON with JavaScript's native JSON.parse
Rift is compiled Rust code. It runs directly on the CPU with:
- No garbage collector - memory is managed at compile time
- No warmup needed - starts at full speed immediately
- Async I/O with Tokio - efficiently uses all CPU cores
- SIMD-optimized JSON parsing that's 10x faster than V8
For JSONPath specifically, Mountebank uses a JavaScript JSONPath library. Rift uses a Rust implementation that's compiled to native code. That's why JSONPath predicates are 247 times faster.
